LESSON: HAND WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.1: Hand Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Hand Writing, part of Writing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why are we supposed to write neatly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise different sounds and syllables from a variety of text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Hand Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write letters, syllables and three letter words neatly and legibly,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Hand Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. discover new ideas related to hand writing.. ● Explains how good handwriting should be. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication. ● Observe charts and books with good hand writing where letters are well shaped, arranged and of good size. ● Observe the shaping of letters from a digital device. ● Read syllables from any available source; digital devices, books, charts. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech to read syllables while those with manipulation difficulties use adapted digital devices or page turners. ● Read three letter words from any available source; digital device, books, charts. Why are we supposed to write neatly? 92 ● Practise writing three letter words collaboratively and later individually. For example; bat, tab, mat / bet, met, pet Learners with manipulation difficulties to use adapted writing tools or adapted digital device ● Display written words for others to read as they are supported. ● Blend sounds and read them aloud as they write them down in books. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tool with books held firmly with a book holder.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Hand Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Hand Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner demonstrates resilience in writing three letter words.

• Unity: The learner interacts with others in striving to achieve the common goal of writing three letter words.

Core competencies:

• Self –efficacy: The learner confidently writes and assertively displays written three letter words.

• Creativity and imagination: The learner skillfully blends syllables and letter sounds to read three letter words.

Values:

• Responsibility: The learner demonstrates resilience in writing three letter words.

• Unity: The learner interacts with others in striving to achieve the common goal of writing three letter words.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issue(
s) :

Effective communication: The learner practises writing neatly three letter words for readability purpose.

Good hand writing is a skill necessary in all other Activity Areas for easy reading and comprehension.
